sources.title: Jonas Peters, Joris Mooij, Dominik Janzing, and Bernhard Schölkopf, Causal Discovery with Continuous Additive Noise Models, Journal of Machine Learning Research 15 (2014)
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete published 45-page JMLR article PDF, not an abstract or landing page.
sources.locator: Section 1.1, Markov property, printed pp. 2010–2011; Section 3 and §3.1–3.2, printed pp. 2014–2025; Theorems 20, 28, 34; Examples 24–26; Appendix A.5 and A.10–A.12, A.15, printed pp. 2040–2048.
sources.read_locator: Inspected the complete ANM setup and causal-minimality statement; the full Condition 19 equation; the complete Appendix A.5 log-density derivation; nondescendant-noise and conditional-minimality arguments in A.10; the complete A.11 conditioning argument and A.12 graph comparison; A.15 sink-search proof; and §1.1 definition of the Markov property. The new density conditional-independence item proves the required ANM implication locally rather than importing a global-Markov proof.
sources.extent: Primary complete proof treatment. The carriers reproduce the necessary arguments locally and make density versions, intermediate conditioning, and edgewise minimality explicit.
sources.support: ANM definition, exact Condition 19, bivariate direction theorem, restricted-ANM condition, density and nondescendant-noise lemmas, conditioned graph comparison, local ANM density-to-d-separation conditional-independence argument, population RESIT, and assigned examples.

contents.name: Section 3, Definition 16 and Proposition 17: continuous ANM and edgewise causal minimality
contents.detail: Printed pp. 2014–2015. Local definition preserves the finite observed DAG, independent positive-density noises, continuous equations, and nonconstancy in each parent coordinate.

contents.name: Equation (6): triangular additive-noise equations
contents.detail: The paper supplies the ANM equations. The local lemma proves the joint product density from independent noise laws and coordinate translations; the citation does not replace that proof.

contents.name: Appendix A.10, Lemma 37: a node noise is independent of every set of nondescendants
contents.detail: Printed p. 2044. The local proof supplies the finite recursive substitution argument from independent exogenous noises.

contents.name: Section 3.1, Definitions 18 and 19: bivariate Condition 19
contents.detail: Printed pp. 2021–2022. The complete differential equation and its nonzero-denominator domain are transcribed and defined locally.

contents.name: Section 3.1, Theorem 20 and Appendix A.5: bivariate direction identifiability
contents.detail: Printed pp. 2022 and 2040–2041. The local proof derives the reverse-model log-density invariant and expands it to the full Condition 19 equation.

contents.name: Appendix A.10, Lemma 38: causal-minimality dependence persists under non-descendant conditioning
contents.detail: Printed p. 2044. The local proof gives the density intersection argument and the shift-identifiability step for nonconstant parent coordinates.

contents.name: Section 4.1, Algorithm 1: RESIT sink ordering and edge pruning
contents.detail: Printed p. 2028. The authored procedure states a deterministic population-oracle form with fixed tie-breaking and an explicit failure result outside its correctness regime.

contents.name: Sections 3.2 and 4.1, Theorems 28 and 34; Appendices A.11 and A.15
contents.detail: Printed pp. 2024–2028 and 2044–2049. The local proof separately proves the conditioned reversed-edge graph lemma, exact-witness sink argument, and edge-pruning criterion; the article gives the source results and a concise proof sketch.

contents.name: Section 3.1, Example 24: reversible linear-Gaussian ANM
contents.detail: Printed p. 2023. The local example fixes unit variances and verifies the backward residual by an exact linear density transformation and product factorization.

contents.name: Section 3.1, Condition 19 and Theorem 20 applied to a cubic Gaussian ANM
contents.detail: The paper gives the criterion, not this parameter choice. The local example substitutes f(x)=x^3 and standard normal densities into the exact equation and computes a violating point.

contents.name: Section 1 discussion of latent variables and Section 3 warning about marginalization
contents.detail: The paper motivates latent-variable limits. The local Gaussian construction separately verifies two equal observational laws with different interventions.

contents.name: Appendix A.12, proof of Proposition 29(i): a conditioned reversed edge for distinct minimal DAGs
contents.detail: Printed pp. 2045–2047. The local finite-graph proof expands the sink reduction and the path-separation case split needed to obtain the exact parent/nondescendant conditioning interface.

contents.name: Appendix A.15, youngest-child conditioning in the false-sink argument
contents.detail: Printed p. 2049. The source uses this conditional-independence step; the local lemma derives its density factorization from the positive ANM product density for every finite positive conditioning section.

contents.name: Appendix A.5, nonperiodicity used in the reverse-density argument
contents.detail: The source uses the density case. The local proof gives the more general probability-measure argument by equal mass on translated intervals.

contents.name: Appendix A.15, residual independence in the false-sink argument
contents.detail: The source uses the residual equation but does not record pointwise density versions. The local lemma proves the smooth shear-density and continuity extension required at a specified restricted-condition witness.

contents.name: Section 1.1: definition of the Markov property for a DAG
contents.detail: The paper defines the graph-level implication from d-separation to conditional independence but does not prove this ANM density case; the local item derives the needed marginal-density factorization from the product density and ancestral moral separation.

sources.title: Jonas Peters, Dominik Janzing, and Bernhard Schölkopf, Elements of Causal Inference, MIT Press (2017)
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted 289-page book PDF; retrieved directly after the browser PDF viewer failed to extract it, then inspected from the full extracted text.
sources.locator: Chapter 4, §4.1.4, Definition 4.4, Theorem 4.5 and proof sketch, printed pp. 49–51; Chapter 7, §7.2.3 for the multivariate ANM/RESIT overview.
sources.read_locator: Read the complete §4.1.4 ANM definition, smoothness hypotheses, derivative condition, and Theorem 4.5 proof sketch, including the explicit statement that the details are in Hoyer et al. Read the §7.2.3 RESIT discussion and its attribution to Mooij et al. and Peters et al.
sources.extent: Independent full-book treatment and primary book source for the ANM vocabulary and smooth bivariate identifiability framing. Its Theorem 4.5 proof is only a sketch, so the local carriers use the full JMLR proof for every omitted derivation.
sources.support: ANM definition, generic bivariate identifiability framing, linear-Gaussian reversible example, and the distinction between population identification and practical fitting.; general restricted-ANM graph identifiability context.

contents.name: §4.1.4, Definition 4.4: an additive-noise representation
contents.detail: The definition agrees with the local equation and independence convention; the local definition additionally fixes the finite observed-DAG scope.

contents.name: §4.1.4, Theorem 4.5 and differential invariant (4.6)
contents.detail: The book states a related generic condition and gives only a proof sketch referring to Hoyer et al. It is corroborating context, not the proof source for the local Condition 19 derivation.

contents.name: §4.1.4, Figure 4.2: linear-Gaussian two-direction example
contents.detail: The local example supplies an exact unit-variance instance and proves independence of the backward residual.

contents.name: §7.2.3: RESIT is a regression-and-independence method for multivariate ANMs
contents.detail: This section is an overview and refers to the paper for correctness; the local algorithm and theorem contain the full procedure and proof.

contents.name: §7.2.3: hidden variables can obstruct observed-only ANM identification
contents.detail: The book supplies the warning. The local example gives a separate exact Gaussian pair of observationally equivalent SCMs and computes their different interventions.

sources.title: K. Assaad, E. Devijver, and G. Gaussier, Causal discovery: noise-based methods, ENS Lyon course notes (2023)
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete 42-slide course-note PDF, not an abstract or excerpt.
sources.locator: Slides 22–23 for the nonlinear ANM condition and latent-variable caveat; slides 29–31 for causal sufficiency/minimality and the two RESIT phases; slides 32–35 for the multivariate walkthrough.
sources.read_locator: Inspected the complete relevant slides. The deck presents the Condition 19 exception as an overview, notes that ANMs are not closed under marginalization, states causal sufficiency and minimality, and prints a two-phase multivariate ANM algorithm. It does not provide the full identifiability or RESIT proofs and is not used as a proof substitute.
sources.extent: Independently authored lecture-note treatment, used for scope cross-checks and the algorithm overview only. The JMLR article supplies the complete proofs.
sources.support: Causal sufficiency warning, the Condition 19 exception at overview level, and RESIT's order-then-prune structure. The additional graph and density prerequisites are proved locally from the complete primary-paper route.

contents.name: Slides 22–23: bivariate ANM reversibility requires the differential-equation exception; marginalization with latent variables can leave the ANM class
contents.detail: The slides are an overview and omit smoothness details; the local definition uses the exact JMLR equation and its domain.

contents.name: Slides 29–31: causal sufficiency, minimality, and the two phases of multivariate ANM search
contents.detail: The slides corroborate the order-then-prune organization; the local algorithm fixes the population oracle, tie rule, and return behavior.

contents.name: Slides 32–35: multivariate sink-selection walkthrough
contents.detail: The example is pedagogical and contains no correctness proof; the local theorem proves sink selection and pruning from the JMLR argument.

contents.name: Slide 23: latent-variable marginalization caveat
contents.detail: The local Gaussian construction verifies the warning with equal observational covariance matrices and distinct intervention means.
